text.p: Amerigon Inc, a development stage company making automotive products, Friday said it expects a combination of lower revenues and higher costs will lead to net losses.

"Revenues for the near future will be significantly less than in prior periods," Lon Bell, chief executive officer, said in a statement. "The company expects to continue to expend substantial funds on its development efforts and to incur losses for the foreseeable future," he added.
Earlier, Amerigon reported a second quarter share loss of $0.25 a share versus a loss of $1.12 a share one year ago.
In a statement, Amerigon said second quarter revenues fell to #350,000 compared with $1.56 million last year. The lower revenues largely stem from the completion of a major electric vehicle contract.
Lastly, the company said it remains excited about the market for its climate controlled automobile seat and radar sensing products, and it continues to receive positive reactions for both.
